So I've been reading the system and I keep seeing flaws in how conflict resolution is being handled,

Theoretically the rule is that 24 hours must pass before the vote is counted. As a result, I am inclined to forbid that the Candid be claimed until that point has passed.

Additionally, actions of players imo should not be open to a vote. Actions should be phrased such that they may be opposed, but they should actually be opposed instead of having people say "Nah... Didn't happen". If no one can write a plausible way to oppose an action they dislike through their godly powers, then it should happen. Otherwise... Well, I'll never get anything done as an apocalyptic deity.

I agree with the actions. It makes sense for creation to be voted on. It prevents someone from making ridiculously strong or non-cannon things.

Actions shouldn't be voted on, but left to the mods to clean game breaking actions.

Currently I'm kinda the GM because it's my decision to include things into the Ecosystem or not. However, not deciding is even worse. Because the flood of change and creation doesn't halt, not even during Sabbath. If I wouldn't add thing until after 24hrs I think most players would be lost as to what happend/happens in our universe.

I agree that "Nah didn't happen" is bad, but it should remain possible to oppose the second coming of Kim Jong Un and trolls of the like and overpowered short pressed actions.

For voting systems I'd like to see the possibility of backdoor voting and conniving (though Phyra offcourse opposes) I'd like [Council] to be called more often to herald the coming of bigger acts/creations. It is indeed unfair to just post "I create X, X is unstoppable" It is however more fair to propose this and only create X a day after the council convened.

I agree that "Plausible" actions should be able to pass regardless. Me creating being of order, though opposed, should happen and be countered by the other gods. Other gods conniving in the deep will happen, regardless of being opposed. But as the system is now, gods feel obliged to vote Nay if the action goes against the core of their god (which is a sound reason).

I propose the Aye or Nay should stand for "Plausible" / "Not Plausible" or for gods to be able to vote [M] Aye as to show that while the action goes against their god, they agree with the action for the universe.

I agree that there's a complete lack of objective A > B. The problem herein is that this world cannot be destilled to an Attack and Defense number like yugioh or magic. What would Keema, goddess of poisons grant to her creations? A virus cannot be destroyed by conventional strength. How will guile and mind control and the such be measured?

I think that the voting system is problematic, because like democracy in real life it doesn't allow for any sort of actions which are destructive to the collective. I understand that you oppose the existence of trolls, but I honestly don't think that an effective villain can exist without some people considering it a troll. The point of having an antagonist is that things will be destroyed. And people will be upset about it, or they can bypass it through ingenuity.

Ok, so for the virus example, I think that that's what moderators are for. Ideally the players identify weaknesses and boundaries of what they do, and allow other players to react accordingly. However, that involves a certain level of trust to allow the players to try and make something interesting work. Basically, if the gods trying to stave off a deadly virus can come up with something that sounds interesting and plausible to all parties, then it should work. In cases that an agreement can't be reached, an arbiter steps in and makes the decision.

On a side note this is part of why I chose the apocalypse. As long as a player with an ability like that avoids being too heavy handed, it can serve as a very useful soft reset.
